original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Prove that t coordinate-SWAP targets cost exactly 3t paid coordinate-CNOT calls in the formal M_R(F2[GL_n(F2)]) model, for every n >= 2 and R >= t, with free scalar mixing and restored dirty registers. This answers PR #4939 open question 1 (three swaps cost nine).
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian register model to escape the three-register obstruction. PR #4939 (pending, head 743ddd6275cfd560d9c3e7825c42545152d14e4c) showed that address spectators do not help two swaps, and asked whether they help three. This package answers that formal-model question negatively for every swap count. It is a negative formal-model screen. It does not satisfy the card's native construction gate.
bottleneck_link: It closes the spectator-coordinate escape for the rank-one coordinate-CNOT tariff in this formal model. Any saving must come from a changed native operation or tariff, not from extra address coordinates.
stop_rule: Stop at the uniform written proof, exact regular-representation checks for n <= 4 and the attaining word. Do not search native operations or other tariffs.
author: James Reed
ai_assistance: Substantial assistance from Anthropic Claude (Claude Code, Opus 5.5).

open_questions.question: Does the row-order cut extend to SWAP targets on different coordinate pairs in different registers, or to other permutation targets (for example 3-cycles of coordinates)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Mixed targets are the next formal-model case where spectators or shared work might lower the per-target cost. The present cut uses one coordinate pair for every register.
open_questions.first_step: For two registers carrying swaps of (0,1) and (1,2) at n = 3, compute the best permutation cut in the regular representation by the same column-generation LP and compare it with the six-call word.
